cells.tense: You are here now, at the edge of the fog, choosing the direction and walking it with your whole weight.
cells.act: listen as a student of it
cells.ask: Sit with something you've already settled and let someone walk through their view of it, all the way, without your leading. Listen as a beginner, for what your answer skipped.
cells.core:
You can move without the whole road being mapped — pick a direction in fog, walk it, and the walking is what makes the ground. That isn't recklessness; it's the kind of leading that works when clarity hasn't arrived. You choose, you move, and moving is itself a way of knowing.

The same sureness that carries you can close a door on what hasn't landed yet. Set something you've already settled back down where you can see it. Not everything — the one you haven't questioned in a while. Give it to someone and take in their account of it as a beginner would, curious about what you might have missed. You will move anyway. You'll move with more in hand.
cells.sheetLine: You move first in the fog, and the path forms under your feet.
cells.verb: catalysing intent — choosing a direction and moving first, so the path exists because you walked it
cells.place: in imagination, where you move through fog with only enough light for the next step

cells.tense: You are firing ahead of the fog now, building the road in your head because you cannot tolerate not seeing the whole of it.
cells.ask: Lay out the next three moves toward something you're pushing at — on paper, specific. Then wait a day before touching move one. Plan fully; act slowly.
cells.core:
You are bracing against a future that can't be written yet, and the bracing has turned into speed. You reason through everything before it arrives, cut to the logic, charge at a door that may not even be the right door — because waiting in fog feels like failing. It doesn't. But the charge has outrun the thing it's charging at.

What's useful is the thinking itself, slowed down. Put the plan somewhere you can see it without acting on it. Three moves written out, then a day of not moving. The logic will hold. You may find move one changes, or that you were solving a problem you hadn't met yet.
cells.sheetLine: You're charging at a fog you haven't let form yet.
cells.verb: catalysing intent — choosing a direction and moving first, so the path exists because you walked it
cells.place: in imagination, where you move through fog with only enough light for the next step

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door you already walked through, waiting for permission that came and went.
cells.act: move the structure one real inch
cells.ask: Choose the smallest real piece of what you keep not starting — a message, one page, a call — and do only that, with no plan for what follows. Stop there and notice you moved.
cells.core:
The moving that used to come naturally has gone quiet. You can still see the direction, you know what you'd do if you were in motion, but the motion isn't happening — and fog that used to be walkable now reads like a wall. Under it, the knack is still in you. It just isn't arriving in the present tense.

Getting it going again isn't a leap. It's a real inch, chosen by you, done without needing to see past it. Take the smallest thing you've been avoiding, do only that, and stop. Not because an inch is enough — because something standing still needs one true thing to happen inside it before the next thing can.

cells.verb: catalysing intent — choosing a direction and moving first, so the path exists because you walked it
cells.place: in imagination, where you move through fog with only enough light for the next step

cells.tense: You are steering a room toward a direction it follows, and you would tell anyone you're just along for the ride.
cells.act: release what is done and keep what serves
cells.ask: Put down in plain sight something you've been carrying because it might still matter — a plan, a project, a role. Leave it there a week and notice what you miss and what you don't.
cells.core:
In fog, the people near you find their way because you've already chosen — quietly, without announcing it — and that sureness is what holds things steady. By your own account you're improvising like everybody else. You're not. The leading is real and it's yours, and you've kept it in a drawer marked not really me.

The cost shows as carrying things past their end, because letting go would mean admitting you were holding them. Pick one you're maintaining out of habit and put it down where you can see it down. Not discarded — released, visibly. What's finished will go quiet. What's alive will call you back.
cells.sheetLine: You're steering the room and calling it the room's own drift.
cells.verb: catalysing intent — choosing a direction and moving first, so the path exists because you walked it

attempts.check: The record supports the card, the seat, and the mechanism links, but not the moment-to-moment texture I'm giving each status — I'm rendering mechanism as recognisable behavior, which is a reading, not a report. A reader could reasonably say 'I don't lead from the front, I hang back' — so each core names the mechanism in general terms the person can confirm or refuse, and the ask stands even if the read misses. The sentence serving me is the one that sounds like insight; I cut it. The ask survives being wrong because it teaches the person something about how they move regardless of whether the status fits.
